cards.text: Hezekiah, king of Judah, just led a Passover in Jerusalem with great rejoicing. Now it's all over, and the Israelites who were there head out into the cities of Judah. And friend, they are NOT heading straight home.

cards.question: The Israelites who just worshiped the LORD in Jerusalem fan out into the cities of Judah. What do they do there?

answers.text: Smash the pillars and tear down the high places
Build new altars on every hilltop
Read the Law aloud at every city gate

cards.question: The Israelites tear down the high places and altars throughout Judah and Benjamin. True or false: they stop there and leave Ephraim and Manasseh alone.

cards.text: They keep going until every last one is destroyed, and THEN they go home, each to his own property. These folks don't do "I'll get to it next weekend." I lived in a junk drawer, friend. I know exactly where next weekend goes.
Back in Jerusalem, Hezekiah puts the divisions of the priests and Levites back in place. Every group gets its own duties again.

cards.question: Hezekiah reestablishes the divisions of the priests and Levites. Which of these duties is on their list?

cards.text: Now, those burnt offerings happen every morning and every evening, plus Sabbaths, New Moons and the appointed feasts. That's a LOT of offerings, friend. Somebody's footing that bill.

cards.question: The regular burnt offerings, morning and evening, Sabbaths, New Moons and feasts, are offered as written in the Law of the LORD. Who covers them?

answers.text: The king from his own possessions
The priests from their own flocks
The officials from the city treasury

cards.text: Then Hezekiah turns to the people living in Jerusalem. He commands them to make a contribution for the priests and Levites.

cards.question: Hezekiah commands the people in Jerusalem to give to the priests and Levites. What is it for?

answers.text: So they can devote themselves to the Law of the LORD
So they can rebuild the walls of Jerusalem
So they can pay the soldiers of the king

cards.text: The order goes out. Now you know how it goes when the office passes around a donation envelope. Suddenly EVERYBODY is real busy with their phone.

cards.question: As soon as Hezekiah's order goes out, the Israelites ___ provide the firstfruits of the grain, new wine, oil and honey.
Hezekiah's order went to the people living in Jerusalem. True or false: they're the only ones who bring gifts.

cards.text: The folks in the cities of Judah bring a tithe of their herds, their flocks and the holy things too, and they lay it all out in large heaps. I fill cookie boxes for a living, friend, and I have NEVER once needed the word heaps.

cards.question: The people start building up the heaps in the third month. When do they finish?

cards.text: Third month to the seventh. That's not a pile, friend, that's a SEASON. Then Hezekiah and his officials come out to see the heaps for themselves.

cards.question: When Hezekiah and his officials view the heaps, they ___ the LORD and His people Israel.

cards.text: Then Hezekiah asks the priests and Levites about all these heaps. Azariah, the chief priest of the household of Zadok, gives him the answer.

cards.question: Azariah tells Hezekiah the priests have had enough to eat with plenty left over. Why, in Azariah's words?

answers.text: The LORD has blessed His people
The harvest came in early this year
The king sent extra from the palace

cards.text: Then Azariah says it: "this great abundance is what is left over." LEFTOVERS! Friend, when I finish a batch, my leftovers are three crumbs and one lonely chocolate chip.

cards.question: With that much left over, Hezekiah commands the priests and Levites to prepare ___ in the house of the LORD.

cards.text: From then on they faithfully bring in the gifts, and Conaniah the Levite runs it all with his brother Shimei and a team of overseers under them. Kore, the Levite who keeps the East Gate, handles the freewill offerings, and his men share out portions to the priests and Levites in their cities, old and young, families included.

cards.question: Hezekiah did all this throughout Judah. How does Scripture sum up what he did before the LORD his God?
True or false: Hezekiah does the work for the house of God with half his heart, just going through the motions.
Hezekiah seeks his God with all his heart in every work he begins. What comes of it?

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave Hezekiah for now. Keep your apron on, friend, because this king's story isn't done.

findings.problem: The card states facts from outside the passage: Hezekiah just led a Passover in Jerusalem with great rejoicing (2 Chronicles 30). The card cites only 2 Chronicles 31:1, so these facts carry no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: This is the setup card for card 12, but its joke points the baker toward the wrong answer. People stalling over a donation envelope suggests the Israelites gave reluctantly, and 'reluctantly' is one of the wrong answers on card 12. Nothing on the card helps the baker reason toward 'generously'. The comparison also has the opposite action from the text, which describes eager giving.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'The LORD has blessed His people', uses Scripture's own wording. The wrong answers ('The harvest came in early this year', 'The king sent extra from the palace') sound casual and modern, so the right answer stands out as the most Bible-sounding.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'Good and upright and true', is fully positive. Both wrong answers ('Bold but often hasty', 'Careful but slow to act') follow a different 'X but Y' pattern with a built-in flaw. The right answer stands out by its form and tone.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The question says Hezekiah seeks his God with all his heart in every work he begins. With that setup, 'He loses his kingdom' and 'He leaves Jerusalem' are not believable outcomes, so the right answer is obvious.

rule.text: Wrong answers for what someone does or says only need to be believable.

findings.problem: The last story card is only the line saying the story isn't over. It tells no part of 2 Chronicles 31:21, but it cites that verse. The docs allow a card that is just this line, but they don't say what a story card that tells no verse should cite.
findings.question: When the final story card is only the 'story isn't over' line, what should its verses field be: the passage's last verse, the whole passage, or something else?
